title: refactor: centralize API-key auth, metadata, and account permissions
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Centralizes API-key loading/status checks and metadata normalization across auth, routes, OAuth, lookup, and billing.
- Centralizes session-aware `account:profile`, `account:usage`, and `account:keys` permission checks.
- Preserves response shapes, permission errors, metadata defaults, session bypass, banned/staging checks, key budgets, BYOP attribution, and agent-run inheritance.
- Removes 134 net lines across 14 files.

Safety fixes and validation:
- Merged current `main` without conflicts.
- Fixed the stale provider-profile call to the removed permission helper; this was the current head’s CI typecheck failure.
- Enter typecheck and production frontend build passed.
- Biome passed on all 13 surviving changed sources (two pre-existing optional-chain warnings only); diff and removed-reference scans passed.
- Focused auth/permissions suite: 97 passed; the same four obsolete-fixture failures reproduce unchanged on `main` because `/api/auth/api-key/create` is intentionally blocked with 405.
- Dedicated expired-key rejection test passed.
- Valid secret/publishable/restricted keys, delegated run tokens, metadata, profile/usage permissions, OAuth, device flow, and quests are covered by the passing tests.
- Fresh exact-head CI and CodeQL are required before merge.

gist.headline: One keyring to rule them
gist.blurb: The hive put its API keys back on one tidy hook. Auth, metadata, and account permissions now share the same set of careful checks instead of growing their own tiny key cupboards.
gist.summary: Centralized API-key loading, status validation, metadata normalization, and session-aware account profile, usage, and keys permissions across Enter auth, OAuth, billing, lookup, device flow, quests, and routes while preserving existing response shapes and key behaviors.
gist.impact: Secret, publishable, and restricted keys, delegated run tokens, expired-key rejection, BYOP attribution, budgets, and account permissions now receive consistent handling throughout the API.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy garden-shed key station represents centralized API-key handling: one labeled keyring routes different key types through orderly paths to profile, usage, billing, OAuth, and device-flow terminals. Polli acts as the observant keeper with a tiny keyring and gardener tool belt, while a CRT monitor robot happily verifies each route; code-plants and flowers make the shared auth layer feel like healthy infrastructure rather than a security bunker.
